s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of fever and generalized skin eruption with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face
Large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
key_facts: Recent hospitalization for photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
Thrombocytopenia with platelet count of 81 K/μL
Hypocomplementemia with C3 of 42 mg/dL and C4 of 3 mg/dL
Positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies
Negative bacterial blood, urine, stool and cerebrospinal fluid cultures
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of SLE and current symptoms are consistent with an SLE flare

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with fever, skin eruption, and target lesions, which are characteristic of SJS

shortlist.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's skin lesions and biopsy results are consistent with TEN

shortlist.label: Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including malar rash and photosensitivity, are consistent with ACLE

shortlist.label: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's skin lesions, including bullae, are consistent with BLE

raw.rationale: The patient's history of systemic lupus erythematosus, recent hospitalization for photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, and presence of erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, along with positive antinuclear antibody and anti-double-stranded DNA titers, support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of SLE, the current presentation is more specific to cutaneous manifestations

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
rejected.why: The presence of target lesions and bullae could suggest SJS, but the patient's history and laboratory findings are more consistent with ACLE

rejected.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not meet the criteria for TEN, which typically involves widespread skin detachment and a higher mortality rate

rejected.label: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has bullae, the overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with ACLE
